name: Irving, James, Arthur
notes: Family entry for K.C. Irving's sons (Irving Oil / J.D. Irving, New Brunswick). All three brothers have died: John E. 'Jack' Irving in 2010, Arthur Irving on May 13, 2024 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Irving), and James K. Irving on June 21, 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Irving).

name: Ronald Southern
notes: ATCO and Spruce Meadows founder Ron Southern died January 21, 2016, in Calgary, aged 85 (https://globalnews.ca/news/2469107/atco-founder-ron-southern-dies-at-85). His daughter Nancy Southern now leads ATCO.

name: Alexander Spanos
notes: Real estate developer and Chargers owner Alex Spanos died October 9, 2018, aged 95 (https://www.kpbs.org/news/2018/oct/09/chargers-owner-alex-spanos-dies-at-95/). His son Dean Spanos is now the Chargers' controlling owner.

name: Djuhar Sutanto
notes: Salim Group co-founder Sutanto Djuhar (Liem Oen Kian) died July 2, 2018, in Fuzhou, China, aged 90 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutanto_Djuhar). His son Tedy Djuhar is on the First Pacific board.

name: Bernard Lewis
notes: River Island founder Bernard Lewis died 28 February 2026, 18 days after his 100th birthday (https://www.jewishnews.co.uk/a-true-gentleman-who-quietly-led-from-the-front-tributes-paid-to-river-island-founder-bernard-lewis/). River Island is now led by his nephew Ben Lewis.

name: Alice N. Schwartz
notes: Bio-Rad co-founder and Director Emeritus Alice Schwartz died September 25, 2025, aged 99 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250929203438/en/Bio-Rad-Laboratories-Inc.-Co-Founder-and-Director-Emeritus-Alice-Schwartz-Passes-Away). Her son Norman Schwartz is Bio-Rad's chairman and CEO.

name: Peter M. Nicholas
notes: Boston Scientific co-founder and former CEO Pete Nicholas died May 14, 2022, aged 80 (https://www.fiercebiotech.com/medtech/boston-scientific-co-founder-former-ceo-peter-nicholas-dies-80).

name: Xie's
notes: Hurun family entry ('Xie family') for Zhongzhi Enterprise Group. Its founder Xie Zhikun died of a heart attack in Beijing on December 18, 2021, aged 61 (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2021-12-19/chinese-tycoon-who-built-zhongzhi-enterprise-group-dies-101819642.html). The group later defaulted and went into bankruptcy liquidation, and some relatives were part of a police investigation. No individual heir is identifiable. Not a viable outreach target.

name: Thomas James
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Raymond James Financial; co-founder of the James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art (St. Petersburg, FL)
profile: Son of Raymond James founder Robert James, Tom James built the firm into a national financial services group over 40+ years as CEO and then chairman. He stepped down as chairman in 2017 and retired from the board in Feb 2024. He now focuses on art: he and his wife Mary opened the James Museum in St. Petersburg in 2018.
interesting_fact: Tom and Mary James have collected 3,000+ works of American, Western and wildlife art since their student days. Part of the collection hangs in the James Museum and the rest at Raymond James headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: He began buying art in the 1960s while at Harvard and playing gigs with a rock band. After a 1980s ski week in Aspen he walked into a gallery planning to buy three or four paintings and left with eight. He calls himself 'artistically inept' and has never tried painting.
notes: Retired from Raymond James. The best warm route is probably the James Museum, which he founded and still identifies with; use its contact form with the 'Press' topic. Raymond James media relations handles corporate inquiries.

name: James Packer
current_role: Private investor (Consolidated Press Holdings family interests); partner in the Nobu Beach Inn / The Beach Club, Barbuda development with Robert De Niro
profile: James Packer inherited and expanded the media and gaming empire of his father Kerry Packer, becoming the largest shareholder of casino operator Crown Resorts. He sold his remaining Crown stake to Blackstone in 2022. He now invests privately, and with Robert De Niro and Daniel Shamoon is developing a Nobu-branded resort and residences on Barbuda, set to open in late 2026 or 2027.
interesting_fact: Packer, Robert De Niro and Daniel Shamoon are building The Beach Club, Barbuda, a Nobu Beach Inn resort and residential community on about 400 acres and two miles of Barbuda's southwest coast, on the former K Club site.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing his HSC at Cranbrook School in Sydney, Packer skipped university and worked as a jackaroo on the family's Newcastle Waters cattle station on the Barkly Tableland in the Northern Territory.
notes: Very private and has no published personal or office contact. Consolidated Press Holdings has no public contact page. The most plausible indirect route is the Barbuda resort's (Nobu Hospitality) press office. He has spoken publicly about his mental health, so avoid that topic in outreach. He gives interviews only rarely, such as a 2024-25 interview with The Nightly.

name: Frank Sobey
current_role: Director, Empire Company Limited (Sobeys parent); President, ECL Properties; founding partner, Creative Destruction Lab Atlantic
profile: Frank C. Sobey is a grandson of Sobeys founder Frank H. Sobey and a son of Bill Sobey. He spent 36 years at Empire Company, retiring as VP Real Estate in 2014, and chaired Crombie REIT and its predecessor until 2019. The Sobey family's fortune sits mainly in Empire/Sobeys, Canada's No. 2 grocer, and he remains an Empire director.
interesting_fact: He is a founding partner of CDL-Atlantic, the Atlantic Canada site of the Creative Destruction Lab startup program, and sits on the board of the Canada-U.S. Fulbright Program.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped down as Crombie REIT chair in 2019, he had chaired it for 13 years and its predecessor Crombie Properties for eight, and said he had been 'connected in one way or another with Crombie' for 40 years.
notes: Hurun lists 'Frank Sobey' for the Sobeys fortune. The founder Frank H. Sobey died in 1985, so this is most likely Frank C. Sobey, though Hurun may be using his name for the wider Sobey family stake in Empire. board@empireco.ca is Empire's published channel to directors, and messages go through the corporate secretary. CDL-Atlantic (an entrepreneurship angle) may be a warmer hook.

name: Charles R. Bronfman
current_role: Retired co-chairman of Seagram; philanthropist (honoree of The Charles Bronfman Prize)
profile: Charles Bronfman, born 1931, is a son of Seagram founder Samuel Bronfman. He spent 50 years at Seagram, retiring as co-chairman in 2001, and was principal owner of the Montreal Expos from their 1968 founding until 1991. He chaired the Andrea and Charles Bronfman Philanthropies for 30 years, co-founded Birthright Israel, and in his 90s still focuses on philanthropy.
interesting_fact: He brought Major League Baseball to Canada as the founding principal owner of the Montreal Expos, the first MLB franchise outside the U.S., and owned the team for about 22 years.
deep_cut_fact: His CRB Foundation came up with the Heritage Minutes, the 60-second Canadian history shorts that first aired on CBC on 31 March 1991. He later co-founded Historica Canada, which still produces them.
notes: He is 95, so an interview may be difficult. There is no published personal or office email. The Charles Bronfman Prize (founded by his children) is the nearest official channel. His 2016 memoir 'Distilled' covers Seagram, the Expos and the Heritage Minutes and is a good hook.

name: Luca Querella
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons S.p.A. (Nasdaq: BSP), Milan
profile: Luca Querella is one of the co-founders of Bending Spoons, the Milan company that buys established apps and internet businesses (Evernote, Meetup, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and rebuilds them on its own tech stack. The company was largely bootstrapped until 2022 and listed on Nasdaq in July 2026, pricing above range at about an $18B valuation. The co-founders keep about 83% of the voting power.
interesting_fact: Before Bending Spoons, the founders met while studying in Copenhagen and built a failed note-taking app called Evertale. A decade later Bending Spoons bought Evernote, the best-known note-taking app.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike his Padua-educated co-founders, Querella is the computer scientist of the group. He earned a computer science degree at the University of Turin and a computer engineering degree at the IT University of Copenhagen.
notes: Keeps a very low public profile. CEO Luca Ferrari does nearly all the interviews. The press office (Christy Keenan, press@bendingspoons.com) is the realistic route, and pitching a founders' conversation may land better than Querella alone. Some Italian sources say he joined the original Copenhagen trio slightly later.

name: Lin Gang
current_role: Chairman, Chief Executive and President, China Medical System Holdings (CMS, HKEX: 867)
profile: Lin Gang (Lam Kong in HK filings) founded China Medical System in the mid-1990s and has led it ever since, building a specialty pharma group that licenses, develops and commercializes innovative drugs in China. The company is listed in Hong Kong (867), and he owns about 47.9% through his wholly owned company Treasure Sea Limited.
interesting_fact: He controls nearly half of a Hong Kong-listed pharma company through a single wholly owned vehicle, Treasure Sea Limited (47.86% per the 2025 annual report), and has been an executive director since December 2006.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a pharma entrepreneur he trained as a doctor: he earned a bachelor's degree in clinical medicine from Zhanjiang Medical College (now Guangdong Medical University) in 1986, and the company highlights his 'clinician experience'.
notes: Romanized as 'Lam Kong' in English filings (Chinese 林刚), so use that name when searching. He is low-profile and gives few interviews. Investor relations sits with CFO Chen Yanling's team (ir@cms.net.cn, published in CMS's ESG report).

name: Navin Engineer
current_role: Founder and co-owner (with wife Varsha), Chemidex Pharma, Egham, Surrey
profile: Kenya-born British pharmacist Navin Engineer founded Chemidex with his wife Varsha in 1981, starting with a pharmacy in Chertsey. In 1999 they sold their 14 shops to Celesio for about £12m and turned Chemidex into a company that acquires and markets prescription drug brands. The couple appear on the Sunday Times Rich List with a multi-billion-pound fortune.
interesting_fact: He was sent from Kenya to London in 1963 to live with an aunt, trained at the London School of Pharmacy, and grew a single Chertsey chemist's shop into a billionaire's pharmaceutical business.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after qualifying was as a Boots pharmacist, which he found 'a little bit like the civil service'. When a visiting area manager asked him for a cup of tea while he was busy dispensing prescriptions, he resigned the same day.
notes: Extremely private. Chemidex has no active public website and no published press or office contact; only a registered office on Companies House, which is not a personal contact. The Rich List entry is shared with his wife Varsha. Chemidex-linked firms have drawn press scrutiny over generic drug pricing, so avoid that in outreach.

name: Chen Ailian
current_role: Founder and Chairwoman, Wanfeng Auto Holding Group (also chairs Zhejiang Wanfeng Auto Wheel), Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Chen Ailian founded an aluminum-wheel factory in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, in 1994 that grew into Wanfeng Auto Holding Group, a supplier of lightweight auto parts to BMW, Mercedes, GM, Ford, Toyota and others. She has expanded it into robotics/welding systems (Paslin), magnesium castings (Meridian), general aviation and eVTOLs. She is the wife of Wanfeng co-founder Wu Liangding.
interesting_fact: Wanfeng has moved from car wheels into flight: it owns light-aircraft maker Diamond Aircraft and in 2025 took over German eVTOL startup Volocopter, an unusually large air-mobility bet for an auto-parts founder.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Wanfeng she worked as a truck driver. In 2023 she was a torchbearer for the Hangzhou Asian Games, and Fortune ranked her No. 74 on its 2025 Most Powerful Women in Asia list.
notes: Romanized as 'Ailian Chen' or 'Ai Lian Chen' in English sources. No published press email was found, and the corporate site wfjt.com was unreachable during research. Mandarin outreach through the group or Zhejiang Wanfeng Auto Wheel (SZSE: 002085) board-secretary office would be more realistic. She is a former NPC deputy and party secretary of the group.

name: Alicia Koplowitz
current_role: Chair and 100% owner, Grupo Omega Capital (Madrid family office); president, Fundación Alicia Koplowitz
profile: Alicia Koplowitz inherited a stake in construction group FCC and sold it to her sister Esther in 1997 for about $800M, putting the proceeds into her own investment group, Omega Capital. Omega has held stakes in Acerinox, Iberdrola, Banco Sabadell and other listed companies, plus hotels (Hospes) and real estate. Her foundation funds child and adolescent psychiatry fellowships abroad.
interesting_fact: Her foundation sends Spanish doctors to train in child and adolescent psychiatry at institutions in the UK and US such as Columbia and Stanford, a long-running niche philanthropy that makes her one of Spain's most important funders of youth mental health.
deep_cut_fact: The first public showing of her private art collection was in Paris, not Spain: 'De Zurbarán à Rothko' at the Musée Jacquemart-André (March-July 2017) showed 53 works from Zurbarán and Goya to Picasso, Modigliani and Rothko.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews. The foundation email is the only published channel; Omega Capital has no public contact. An outreach note in Spanish would help. Avoid family and divorce topics.

name: Simon Nixon
current_role: Private investor (Simon Nixon family office); owner of SimonEscapes luxury villa rentals; co-founder of Moneysupermarket.com
profile: Simon Nixon co-founded price-comparison site Moneysupermarket in 1993, floated it in 2007 and sold his last shares in 2016. He has since backed dozens of startups, including Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise before their IPOs, and runs SimonEscapes, which rents out his luxury homes in places such as Malibu and Barbados. He is based in Jersey.
interesting_fact: He was an early private investor in Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise (TransferWise) before they went public, and has put more than £100m into startups since leaving Moneysupermarket.
deep_cut_fact: Moneysupermarket began in 1993, while Nixon was an accounting student at Nottingham, as 'Mortgage 2000', an offline service selling mortgage information to independent financial advisers. It became moneysupermarket.com in 1999.
notes: SimonEscapes is his own business, so its inbox is the closest published route, though it is a bookings address. He has given interviews to City AM and the Chester Chronicle and is relatively accessible for a billionaire. His startup investing (an angel-investor angle) is a natural podcast hook. Avoid the Jersey tax-move topic.

name: Sam Goi
current_role: Executive Chairman, Tee Yih Jia Food Manufacturing; Chairman, PSC Corporation; Singapore's non-resident ambassador to Brazil
profile: Fuqing-born Sam Goi, Singapore's 'Popiah King', bought the small spring-roll-pastry maker Tee Yih Jia in 1977 and automated it into one of the world's largest makers of popiah skins and frozen Asian foods (Spring Home, Happy Belly). He also holds property interests through listed GSH and KOP, chairs consumer-goods firm PSC, and opened a S$450m factory in 2023.
interesting_fact: He is Singapore's non-resident ambassador to Brazil, an unusual diplomatic role for a frozen-food tycoon. He was named Singapore's Businessman of the Year (2013) at the Singapore Business Awards.
deep_cut_fact: When he took over Tee Yih Jia in 1977 it was a semi-mechanised spring-roll-pastry factory on Kim Yan Road. By 1989 its spring roll pastry had won a Monde Selection Gold Medal, and in 2000 TYJ ranked No. 1 in Singapore's Enterprise 50 Awards.
notes: tyj@tyjfood.com is Tee Yih Jia's general corporate email, as published. He is fairly accessible to Singapore media and speaks at business events. His youngest son died in 2019, so avoid family topics.
